tool.name: AddRandomNumbers

summary.para:
View online help files: https://www.jennessent.com/data-tools/add-random-numbers.html
Fills a numeric field of a layer's or table's records -- only the selected records when there is a selection, and only the records a definition query shows -- with a constant, a random permutation of 1 to N (every record a different number: the classic way to assign treatments to plots at random), random integers within a range, random decimals between 0 and 1 or within a range, or draws from a normal distribution with a given mean and standard deviation. A missing field is created (integer or double precision as the values need). A seed makes the result repeatable. A port of the CropCentric Add Random Numbers tool (Jenness and Wiebers 2018). Works at every license level.

tool.usage:
Which records. A map layer or table view writes only the records it shows: its selection, if any, and its definition query are honored. A dataset path writes every record. N, for the permutation, is the number of records written.
The values: • Constant value -- the same number in every record. • Random permutation of 1 to N -- the numbers 1..N dealt out in random order, each used once (treatment numbers, random plot order, random visit order). • Random integers within a range -- each record an independent whole number from lowest to highest, inclusive (repeats allowed). • Random decimals between 0 and 1 -- uniform on [0, 1). • Random decimals within a range -- uniform between lowest and highest. • Random decimals from a normal distribution -- Gaussian draws with the given mean and standard deviation.
The field. An existing numeric field is written in place; integer fields take only the integer modes (and a whole-number constant). A name that does not exist yet is created as a LONG field for integer values or a DOUBLE field for decimals (shortened to ten characters on a shapefile or dBASE table).
Repeatability. Give a seed to get the same numbers again; leave it empty for a fresh draw each run.

dialogReference.para: The layer, table view, feature class or table whose records are written. A layer's selection and definition query are honored.

param.name: field
param.displayname: Field to fill (an existing numeric field, or a new field name)

dialogReference.para: The field to write. An existing numeric field is filled in place; a new name is created (integer or double precision to suit the values).

Constant value; Random permutation of 1 to N (each record unique); Random integers within a range; Random decimals between 0 and 1; Random decimals within a range; or Random decimals from a normal distribution (mean, standard deviation).
The value for the Constant value mode.
For the range modes (inclusive for integers).

param.name: sd
param.displayname: Standard deviation of the normal distribution

dialogReference.para: For the normal-distribution mode; cannot be negative.

param.name: seed
param.displayname: Random seed (optional; repeats the same numbers)

dialogReference.para: Any whole number. The same seed with the same records gives the same numbers again.
The input, after writing (for ModelBuilder chaining).

scriptExample.title: Add Random Numbers example (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: Deal the treatment numbers 1..N to the plots of replication 2 in random order.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path arcpy.management.MakeFeatureLayer(r"D:\data\trial.gdb\Plots_2026", "plots") arcpy.management.SelectLayerByAttribute("plots", "NEW_SELECTION", "Rep = 2") arcpy.jenness.AddRandomNumbers( in_table="plots", field="Treatment", mode="Random permutation of 1 to N (each record unique)", seed=42)
